- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially after dips.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias in next 3–5 periods.
- Model consistently overestimates in early forecast horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75–80), model often fails to recognize — apply downward bias and reduce slope of forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- If model forecast is >85% of recent 18-day average, consider downward correction — especially if sentiment is weak or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion — apply smoothing or exponential decay to forecast curve.
